name: Redensity

lead: Redensity is the name Teoxane uses for several hyaluronic acid products. RHA Redensity is a 'resilient' filler for dynamic areas such as the lines around the mouth, and Teosyal PureSense Redensity 2 is used in the tear trough under the eyes to soften hollows.

The gel adds support and hydration where it is placed, so creases look smoother and the under-eye area looks less hollow. A randomised, evaluator-blinded multicenter study of RHA Redensity for moderate-to-severe perioral lines ran 52 weeks against a no-treatment control, and a prospective observational study looked at Redensity 2 around the eyes.

paras: A clinician injects the gel under or into the skin of the target area, often the perioral lines or tear trough, and the smoothing is visible right away. The RHA range is described as stretching and returning with facial movement, and treatments are repeated as the gel gradually breaks down.

Typical effects of hyaluronic acid fillers include swelling, bruising and lumps, with vascular and delayed inflammatory reactions rarer. Hyaluronic acid filler can be dissolved with hyaluronidase, and a 2023 study tested how 21 fillers respond to it.

chain: HA gel fills lines and hollows
angle.text: Teoxane's Redensity hyaluronic acid gels smooth lines around the mouth and soften under-eye hollows, with the change visible as soon as the gel is placed. A randomised 52-week trial studied RHA Redensity for perioral lines.

lead: Redensity is a name used by Teoxane for hyaluronic acid (HA) products, including RHA Redensity (a 'resilient' HA filler) and Teosyal PureSense Redensity 1 and 2.[1][2][3] They are used to soften lines around the mouth and smile, and to fill the hollow under the eye (the tear trough), so the face looks smoother and more rested without surgery.[1][3]

A randomised, evaluator-blinded multicenter study of RHA Redensity for moderate-to-severe dynamic perioral rhytides ran for 52 weeks against a no-treatment control; at week 8 the responder rate by a proprietary scale was 80.7 percent with treatment against 7.8 percent for control, and 66 percent of treated participants were still responders at week 52.[1] A prospective observational study of Redensity 2 in the periorbital region reported real-world efficacy and safety in 136 enrolled subjects, with Global Aesthetic Improvement Scale improvement above 70 percent for the tear trough and other periorbital indications.[3]

The name covers different products: RHA Redensity is the injectable for dynamic lines, Teosyal Redensity 2 is used for the tear trough, and Redensity 1 is a non-crosslinked skin-quality gel that has also been tested in the laboratory as a cell carrier in burn management.[3][4][5]
infobox: Perioral lines, tear trough, crow's feet, radial cheek lines, neck lines
RHA Redensity, Teosyal PureSense Redensity 1 and 2

paras: RHA Redensity is described as a resilient HA filler made with a process intended to preserve HA's natural structure so the gel stretches and returns with facial movement, making it suited to dynamic areas such as the perioral region.[1][6] A 2026 paper on a newer RHA gel compares it against the existing US-approved and CE-marked RHA fillers (RHA 1 to 4 in Europe and RHA Redensity, RHA 2, RHA 3 and RHA Dynamic Volume in the US), describing a crosslinking approach that avoids high chemical modification.[6]

Teosyal PureSense Redensity 2 is described as having a ten-year record for the tear trough, and Teosyal Redensity [I] is a non-stabilised HA gel combined with 14 bioactive ingredients (amino acids, antioxidants, minerals and vitamins) used for skin-quality treatment.[3][5]

Wikipedia describes HA as one of the most common filler materials because it is found naturally in vertebrates and is biodegradable; most HA fillers are crosslinked, usually with BDDE, which slows enzymatic breakdown and lengthens how long they last, and HA gives immediate volume rather than stimulating collagen.[7] In the US fillers are regulated as medical devices and must be injected by a provider, while many more are on the market in Europe where a CE mark does not require demonstration of efficacy, according to the same article.[7]

The perioral region is highly mobile, so lines around the mouth change with speech and expression. The 52-week trial (NCT03092219, n=202) used the Perioral Rhytids Severity Rating Scale and the Global Aesthetic Improvement Scale rated by blinded evaluators, plus self-assessment with FACE-Q.[1][8] Most adverse events were common treatment responses after perioral injection.[1] Anaesthetic-containing versions have been tested in registered studies.[9][10]

In the periorbital observational study, 958 initial injections were given to 136 participants, of which 451 used Redensity 2: tear trough 89, palpebromalar groove 61, outer canthus 45, crow's feet 38 and brow 19.[3] A separate registered trial compared RHA Redensity Eye against no treatment for infra-orbital hollows (NCT04577898, n=248), and a micro-needle device trial tested Redensity [I] on crow's feet.[11][12]

A retrospective controlled ultrasound study of 20 women aged 30 to 42 gave a single cannula-delivered injection of Redensity [I] in the midface, comparing with seven untreated controls, and reported a significant increase in skin density on ultrasound at 3 to 4 weeks.[5] Other registered work covers radial cheek lines and neck and smile lines.[13][14] Laboratory work on non-crosslinked Redensity 1 reported support of keratinocyte and fibroblast viability and collagen deposition as a possible cell carrier for burn wounds.[4]

The 52-week randomised perioral study compared RHA Redensity with no treatment.[1] A prospective observational study assessed Teosyal PureSense Redensity 2 in tear trough and other periorbital areas in routine practice.[3] A retrospective controlled ultrasound study examined cannula-assisted delivery of an HA-based hydrogel for facial skin density.[5]

Registered trials include perioral rhytids,[8] infra-orbital hollows versus no treatment,[11] crow's feet with a micro-needle device,[12] radial cheek lines,[13] neck lines, perioral lines and smiling lines,[14] and anaesthetic-containing versions.[9][10]

Wikipedia lists common effects of HA fillers as bruising, redness, pain and itching, with infection, allergic reactions and lumps less common, and vascular embolization causing blindness or skin necrosis as rare but serious events.[7] In a 2023 in-vitro study, 21 HA fillers were exposed to recombinant human hyaluronidase; RHA 1/Redensity was among the least resistant to dissolving, while RHA 4 was among the most resistant.[2] Clinical safety in the Redensity trials is reported as common treatment responses and adverse events.[1][3]

timeline.event: Registered trial of Redensity [I] with a micro-needle device for crow's feet begins.[12]
RHA Redensity perioral rhytids trial begins (NCT03092219).[8]
Trial of RHA Redensity Eye for infra-orbital hollows begins.[11]
Periorbital real-world and cannula skin-density studies published.[3][5]
